name: Sir Almroth Wright
summary: British immunologist and bacteriologist known for opsonin theory and vaccine therapy.

name: St Mary's Hospital
summary: London teaching hospital where Wright headed bacteriology and pathology departments.

name: Inoculation Department
summary: Research unit founded by Wright at St Mary's Hospital for vaccine therapy.

name: George Bernard Shaw
summary: Irish playwright and personal friend of Wright who modeled a character on him.

name: Sinclair Lewis
summary: American novelist whose work Arrowsmith depicted immunology differently than Shaw.

name: Paul DeKruif
summary: Physician and researcher who collaborated with Lewis and criticized Rockefeller Institute.

name: Jacques Loeb
summary: Physiologist at Rockefeller Institute whose mechanistic philosophy influenced DeKruif.

name: Alexander Fleming
summary: Bacteriologist who worked in Wright's laboratory and discovered penicillin.

name: London
summary: Capital city of the United Kingdom where St Mary's Hospital is located.

name: The Doctor's Dilemma
summary: Play by George Bernard Shaw featuring a character based on Wright.

name: Arrowsmith
summary: Novel by Sinclair Lewis depicting a scientist fighting false theories of immunity.

name: anti-typhoid vaccine
summary: Vaccine developed by Wright to prevent typhoid in soldiers.
